question: How many days of annual leave do full-time employees get?
expected_answer: 28 days a year, including bank holidays (more with long service, up to 30).
ai_answer: Full-time employees get 28 days of paid annual leave each leave year, including bank holidays (Annual Leave Policy §2-4 and Employee Handbook §5-7). Extra days are given for long service: 1 extra day brings the total to 29, and after 5 years' continuous service it is 2 extra days, for 30 in total, which is the maximum. The passage describing the service length for the first extra day is cut off, so the exact threshold for that day is not stated in the passages provided.

question: When do we get paid?
expected_answer: Monthly, on the last working day of the month.
ai_answer: Employees are paid monthly on the last working day of the month, according to the Employee Handbook (v3.2, §4-6 / §5-7 Pay). Payslips are available in StaffHub.

question: How long is the probation period for new starters?
expected_answer: 6 months, with reviews at 3 and 6 months; can be extended by up to 3 months.
ai_answer: New employees have a 6-month probation period. Managers hold review meetings at 3 months and 6 months, and probation may be extended by up to 3 months if more time is needed. During probation, the notice period on either side is 1 week.

question: What is the mileage rate if I use my own car for work?
expected_answer: 45p per mile (normal commuting can't be claimed).
ai_answer: If you use your own car for work, mileage is paid at 45p per mile under the Expenses Policy (v2025.1, §2-3). Normal commuting to your usual workplace cannot be claimed.

question: How long does my password need to be?
expected_answer: At least 14 characters, with MFA wherever supported.
ai_answer: Passwords must be at least 14 characters long, according to the Information Security Policy (v2025.1, effective 1 Mar 2025), section 4-6 Passwords and sign-in. Passwords must also never be shared, written down or reused across systems.

question: How quickly must a customer complaint be acknowledged?
expected_answer: Within 2 working days (final response within 8 weeks).
ai_answer: A customer complaint must be acknowledged within 2 working days. This deadline is shown in the Timescales table of the Customer Complaints Procedure (§5-7) and repeated in the Disputes about a game section (§4-5). The passages are partly cut off, so the full table is not visible.

question: How much company sick pay do I get if I've worked here for 4 years?
expected_answer: 4 weeks at full pay in any rolling 12 months (after probation), on top of SSP.
ai_answer: With 4 years' service you get 4 weeks of sick pay at full pay. This falls in the 3 to 5 years band. After probation, company sick pay tops up SSP to full basic pay, based on length of service, in any rolling 12-month period. Note that the passage containing the company sick pay table is cut off, so the 3 to 5 years row is taken from the sick pay table in the other passage.

question: What support can I get for studying a qualification?
expected_answer: Course fees up to £1,000 a year and up to 5 days' paid study leave, after probation.
ai_answer: Employees who have passed probation can apply for study support for a qualification relevant to their role. This covers course fees of up to £1,000 per year and up to 5 days of paid study leave per year for exams and study. Applications are made through LearnHub and must be approved by the line manager and the Head of Learning and Development. Travel and accommodation for approved training are claimed under the Expenses Policy, and course fees are paid directly by the company rather than claimed as expenses. If you leave within 12 months of a course finishing you must repay 100% of the course fees, and if you leave between 12 and 24 months after it finishes you must repay 50%; the passages provided are partly cut off, so the full repayment terms may not be completely shown.

question: If I leave 18 months after the company paid for my course, do I have to pay anything back?
expected_answer: Yes, 50% of the course fees (leaving between 12 and 24 months after the course).
ai_answer: Yes, probably. Under the Training and Development Policy, if you leave between 12 and 24 months after the course finishes, you must repay 50% of the course fees. The policy measures this from when the course finishes, not from when the company paid, so check your course end date. Passage P2 also covers this rule but is cut off before it states the 12 to 24 month figure, so the 50% rate comes from P1.

question: Is there an allowance for working from home?
expected_answer: £26 a month for employees contracted to work remotely at least 1 day a week.
ai_answer: Yes. Employees whose contract says they work remotely at least 1 day a week receive a home working allowance of £26 a month, paid through payroll.

question: Can I roll over unused holiday into next year?
expected_answer: Yes, up to 8 days, which must be used by 30 June.
ai_answer: Yes, up to 8 days of unused annual leave can be carried forward into the next leave year without approval, but they must be used by 30 June of the new leave year or they are lost and not paid (P3). In exceptional cases up to 20 days may be carried forward, but only if the exception has been approved in writing; sickness-related carried-forward days must be used within 18 months of the end of the leave year they were earned, and other exceptional days by 30 June (P2). The passages are partly cut off, so the full wording of the exception conditions and who approves them is not clear from these extracts.

question: I clicked a dodgy link in an email. What should I do?
expected_answer: Report it to the IT Service Desk immediately (and use Report Phish for suspicious emails).
ai_answer: Do not click any further links or open attachments. Report the email using the Report Phish button in Outlook, and because you have already clicked a link, report it to the IT Service Desk immediately (through StaffHub or on extension 4357). If you entered your password, also report that to the IT Service Desk immediately.

question: Can I keep the tips a punter gives me at the blackjack table?
expected_answer: No. Gaming staff tips go in the tronc box and are shared through the tronc scheme.
ai_answer: No. Gaming employees must never keep tips personally. All tips given to gaming employees are placed in the tronc box at the table and shared through the tronc scheme (Code of Conduct §3-4). Hospitality employees follow their own venue's tipping process instead.

question: I'm too poorly to work my shift on the casino floor. How early do I need to ring in?
expected_answer: At least 2 hours before the shift starts, by phone to the line manager or duty manager.
ai_answer: Gaming floor, security and cage employees must call at least 2 hours before the start of their shift so that cover can be arranged (Sickness Absence Policy §2). You must also call again each day you are absent unless your manager says otherwise, though the rest of that sentence is cut off in the passage provided.

question: How quickly do I have to report a lost company laptop?
expected_answer: Immediately, and in any case within 1 hour, to the IT Service Desk.
ai_answer: A lost or stolen company device must be reported to the IT Service Desk immediately, and in any case within 1 hour of noticing it. The Incident Reporting Procedure also lists lost devices under IT and data as requiring a report to the IT Service Desk within 1 hour, so the 1-hour limit applies. Reporting quickly allows the device to be wiped remotely.

question: What happens to my annual leave if I'm ill while I'm on holiday?
expected_answer: With a fit note, those days count as sickness and the leave is given back. Report it on day one.
ai_answer: If you become ill during booked annual leave and provide a fit note covering the days of sickness, those days are treated as sickness absence and the annual leave is returned to you. You must report the sickness on the first day, following section 2 of the Sickness Absence Policy. The passages do not say how the fit note must be provided beyond this, so check the rest of the policy for that detail.

question: Where do I report a customer I think is laundering money?
expected_answer: Directly to the MLRO with the internal suspicious activity report form, not SafeLog; never tell the customer.
ai_answer: Report it directly to the Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) using the internal suspicious activity report form. The Compliance Guidelines say to send the form directly to the MLRO on the same day, and not to investigate yourself or tell the customer, as tipping off is a criminal offence.

question: Can I claim my course fees back on expenses?
expected_answer: No. Course fees are paid directly by the company under the Training Policy.
ai_answer: No. Course fees cannot be claimed on expenses. Training course fees are paid directly by the company under the Training and Development Policy and are listed as non-claimable in the Expenses Policy (P1, P2). Only travel and accommodation for approved training are claimed through the Expenses Policy (P1).

question: Someone on the gaming floor looks under 18. What do I do?
expected_answer: Ask for photo ID (Think 25), tell the duty manager immediately, and log it before the end of the shift.
ai_answer: Ask the person for valid photo ID under Think 25, and tell the duty manager immediately. Log it in SafeLog before the end of your shift. Nobody under 18 may enter the gaming floor.

question: I was off sick for months last year and couldn't use my leave. How much can I carry over and by when?
expected_answer: Up to 20 days because of long-term sickness, to be used within 18 months of the end of that leave year.
ai_answer: Under the Annual Leave Policy, you can carry forward up to 20 days only if you could not take your leave because of long-term sickness, maternity, paternity, adoption or shared parental leave, or business reasons where your manager cancelled approved leave and the Head of People approved the exception in writing. Days carried forward because of sickness must be used within 18 months of the end of the leave year in which they were earned. The passages do not say how this applies to your specific leave year, and they do not confirm whether your absence counts as long-term sickness or whether you have written approval, so check those with your manager or HR.

question: Can gaming floor staff take two weeks off over Christmas?
expected_answer: No. 24 Dec to 1 Jan is a peak period; at most 5 consecutive days, and only with the General Manager's approval.
ai_answer: Not as a single block of two weeks. Christmas falls within the peak period (24 December to 1 January), and during peak periods gaming floor and security employees may take no more than 5 consecutive days of leave, and only with approval from the General Manager of their venue. Leave also must be booked at least as far ahead as the passages require (for example, 5 days of leave needs at least 10 days' notice), and requests made after the rota is published can only be approved if cover is available. The passages do not say whether two separate blocks of leave over the peak period are allowed, so that part is not covered.

question: How much notice do I need to give to book a week of annual leave?
expected_answer: Twice the length of the leave, so 10 days for 5 days of leave; later if the rota is already published.
ai_answer: You must give notice of at least twice the length of the leave requested, made through StaffHub. For a week (5 working days) of leave, that means at least 10 days before the first day of leave. Leave requested after a gaming floor or security rota is published can only be approved if cover is available, and during peak periods (24 December to 1 January and the weekends of major sporting events listed on the intranet) approval also depends on cover being available. Managers should respond within 5 working days.

question: How much annual leave can I carry forward?
expected_answer: Up to 8 days, used by 30 June (the 2024 rule of 5 days by 31 March no longer applies).
ai_answer: Employees can normally carry forward up to 8 days of unused annual leave into the next leave year, and no approval is needed for this. Carried-forward days must be used by 30 June of the new leave year, or they are lost and not paid. In exceptional cases, up to 20 days may be carried forward, but only if the employee could not take their leave because of long-term sickness, maternity, paternity, adoption or shared parental leave, or business reasons where their manager cancelled approved leave and the Head of People approved the exception in writing. Days carried forward because of sickness must be used within 18 months of the end of the leave year in which they were earned; other exceptional carry-forward must be used by 30 June.

question: How many days a week can office staff work from home?
expected_answer: Up to 2 days with manager agreement; Tuesday and Wednesday are office days (not 3, as in 2023).
ai_answer: The passages do not set a maximum number of days a week that office staff can work from home. They also say Tuesday and Wednesday are anchor days when office-based employees are expected to be in the office, unless they are on leave or have agreed otherwise with their manager. Employees agree their working pattern with their team but must be reachable during the team's agreed working hours.
